newsitem.title: MEXICO: Witnesses tie Raul Salinas to drug traffickers.
newsitem.headline: Witnesses tie Raul Salinas to drug traffickers.

text.p: A Swiss prosecutor has told Raul Salinas, the jailed brother of a former Mexican president, that witnesses in the United States have tied him to drug traffickers, the Swiss government said on Friday.

The Mexican government issued a statement on behalf of Switzerland's Attorney General Carla del Ponte, who spent several days this week in Mexico City questioning Salinas, brother of former President Carlos Salinas de Gortari.

"The prosecutor Del Ponte made known to Raul Salinas de Gortari that there are various witnesses in the United States, who have been questioned by her, that have said he was tied to narco-traffickers," the statement said.

Switzerland has been investigating Raul Salinas ever since an $84 million secret bank account was discovered and its assets frozen in late 1995. Several more of his accounts were discovered later in Switzerland and elsewhere.
Salinas' lawyers reiterated on Friday that their client's Swiss money was not linked to drugs and was instead from a trust fund that belonged to several prominent Mexican industrialists.
But the statement by the Swiss government was the first time it has confirmed that witnesses have tied Raul Salinas to drug traffickers.
A former government official, Salinas is in a maximum-security jail near Mexico City on charges of murder and illicit enrichment. Last week, Mexico also brought money laundering charges against him.
Valentin Roschacher, director of Switzerland's anti-drug police, and chief prosecutor del Ponte, were in Mexico on March 31 to April 4 to question Salinas.
The Miami Herald said on Thursday Swiss authorities believe at least $100 million in Salinas' Swiss bank accounts came from payoffs by a leading drug baron during Carlos Salinas' 1988-1994 term.

Salinas' lawyers dispute this, saying much of the money in the accounts belonged to Mexican business tycoons, including telecommunications magnate Carlos Peralta and Roberto Gonzalez, founder of tortilla firm Grupo Industrial Maseca SA.

Peralta admitted last year that he gave $50 million to Raul Salinas, a charge that sparked charges by Mexico's opposition that the businessmen had bribed Raul during his brother's administration in return for government favours.
